entries.assumptions: determinism; reversibility of the selected representative; maximal-entropy SELECTION of the counting measure among invariant measures — not uniqueness from invariance
entries.note: The scope wall is respected in both directions. REVERSIBILITY IS NOT DERIVED: the manuscript's own status remark calls the bijective substratum a representation choice recovered by a two-pronged argument one prong of which is empirical, so phi is a hypothesis (Equiv.Perm S) everywhere and no theorem concludes that the substratum is bijective; what IS proved from finiteness is the structural prong, injective_imp_bijective. And the selection principle is not silently upgraded to uniqueness: invariance_does_not_select is a THEOREM -- two disjoint nonempty invariant sets carry two distinct invariant probability laws -- with two_cycle_witness supplying the double transposition so it is not vacuous. Orbit uniqueness, invariance of the counting measure, and its entropy maximality are the other three clauses. The manuscript's parenthetical support for the selection reading is a CONTINUUM statement about Liouville measure; it lies outside the framework's finite scope and is not formalized, its role being discharged by the finite non-selection theorem, which the probe checks exhaustively over all 873 permutations of up to six states (invariant-subspace dimension = cycle count).

entries.label: (stochastic inverse)
entries.assumptions: a finite square stochastic matrix with a one-sided stochastic inverse
entries.note: Closed in b448, rank 1 of the backlog, from P. The proof is the manuscript's own, step for step: vanishing off-diagonal entries of A*B force every row of B indexed by the support of a row of A to be a basis vector; two such rows would coincide, which a nonzero determinant forbids; so each row of A carries a single unit entry and the occupied columns are distinct. Both sides of "left or right" are covered without separate proofs, because a one-sided inverse of a square matrix over a commutative ring is two-sided. The countercontrol in the companion probe shows the hypothesis is load-bearing: [[1/2,1/2],[0,1]] is stochastic and invertible and is NOT a permutation, its inverse simply failing to be stochastic.

The third is the one that could have been quietly dropped, and it is where Mathlib earns its place rather than being incidental — extending an isometry to a unitary is orthonormal-basis extension, a real theorem and not bookkeeping. The companion probe checks the two computational clauses on the SQUARED amplitudes so the arithmetic stays rational and no square root is ever approximated, and exhibits an explicit Gram-Schmidt completion for the third. Its countercontrol records that the stochasticity is used in one direction only: for a COLUMN-stochastic T the isometry clause is false.

entries.label: (diagonal preservation)
entries.note: Closed in b448, rank 3 of the backlog, from GAP. DERIVED from permutation unitarity rather than recomputed, as the ordering intends: the only new content is that conjugating by a permutation matrix is a RELABELLING of indices, after which diagonality survives because a permutation is injective and the partial trace of a diagonal state is diagonal. The hidden prior enters as a STATE built from a distribution, Matrix.diagonal mu — which is what mu_H is in the framework (Main section 3.4 writes it as rho_anc = sum_h mu_H(h)|h><h|), so its diagonality is definitional and not an extra hypothesis. The companion probe's countercontrol shows a NON-permutation unitary destroys diagonality, matching the manuscript's own scope remark that the CP-indivisibility reduction fails for a general CPTP family.

entries.label: (C3 necessity)
entries.note: Kernel-proved as a COROLLARY of the hidden-memory layer rather than a second data-processing argument: HiddenMemory.capacity_floor_of_fun bounds the conditional information of ANY quantity read off (X_t, H_t) by log2|C_H|, and c3_necessity instantiates it at the whole visible future while capacity_floor instantiates it at the next visible value, so Lean checks the dependency between the two manuscript theorems. X_>t is DEFINED by iterating the bijection, which is where determinism enters. The corollary's I* is the maximum over a finite nonempty family of accessible slices sharing ONE hidden alphabet -- that sharing is what makes m >= 2^(I*) a statement about a single hidden sector, and it is written into the signature. entries.label: (finite-horizon stochastic–reversible–unitary equivalence)
entries.assumptions: finite visible alphabet; finite accessible horizon K
entries.note: THE CENTRAL EQUIVALENCE CHAIN. Kernel-proved as three explicit constructions -- S_imp_D's multi-time clock-and-record carrier over an arbitrary finite-horizon joint law, D_imp_Qfb's permutation unitary with fixed-basis readout at every time, Qfb_imp_S's chain normalization from unitarity -- assembled by the named wrapper finite_horizon_equivalence, which takes NONE of the three as a hypothesis. The three classes are separate predicates and none is defined through another. TWO SCOPE GUARDS, recorded in the Lean header: the hidden-predictive-memory theorem is neither an assumption nor a lemma here (the equivalence is existential and holds for Markov laws too), and the one-step ancilla dilation of EquivalenceChain.lean does not prove S => D. The class (Q_fb) is defined without an autonomous-generator clause, so the manuscript's U = exp(-iH) remark is a property of the construction and is deliberately left unformalized; widening the class definition is what would reopen this.

entries.label: (unavoidable hidden predictive memory)
entries.assumptions: ANY faithful deterministic realization — the quantifier is the content
entries.note: Closed in b448, rank 1 of the backlog, from P. ALL THREE CLAUSES: the pushforward identity, the distinguishability floor, and the capacity floor M_t <= I(X_<t; H_t | X_t) <= log2 |C_H|. Clause (c) required BUILDING A FINITE SHANNON LAYER, since Mathlib carries no entropy of a finite distribution, no mutual information, no conditional mutual information and no data-processing inequality; OIBridge/FiniteEntropy.lean supplies them from one analytic input, log x <= x - 1. Proving only M_t <= log2|C_H| would have been a different theorem wearing this one's name. The next visible value is DEFINED as the visible component of the bijection rather than assumed to be a function of the pair, so the Markov chain X_<t -> H_t -> X_{t+1} given X_t is a consequence and not a hypothesis. THIS THEOREM IS DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM THE EQUIVALENCE CHAIN and is not a lemma of it: the equivalence is existential and holds for Markov laws too, which is exactly why it cannot do this theorem's work. Each clause has a countercontrol removing the hypothesis its proof consumes — a stochastic channel for (a), a non-TV distance for (b), and a broken Markov chain for (c).

backlog_policy: LEAN-FIRST. Every established canonical mathematical result is a kernel-formalization target by default. GAP IS A BACKLOG STATE AND NOT AN ACCEPTABLE TERMINAL VERIFICATION STATE. An exception requires a RECORDED REASON -- empirical input, an external literature premise, a physical assumption, or a formal library result that does not yet exist -- and even then Lean should prove the implication FROM that premise wherever possible: A_1 and ... and A_n implies the framework conclusion, which is exactly where the framework's own deduction ends and an external assumption begins. Formalization order: central OI/equivalence chain, foundational OI lemmas, existing ROADMAP gaps, reconstruction/representation, comb/locality, GR/SM deductions, then secondary corollaries and controls. WITHIN each tier take the easy K3 conversions first so coverage rises quickly, but NEVER let that displace a central theorem merely because it is harder. And the probes are preserved after Lean catches up: the standard is Lean theorem PLUS independent executable probe PLUS countercontrols, never Lean instead of probes.

backlog.route: Not derivable as stated -- it is a premise. The kernel-checkable content is the IMPLICATION from a finite-area boundary and a finite mode count to a finite visible alphabet, with the holographic bound left as a named external hypothesis.

ROADMAP A5-B22. Blocked on a Mathlib lemma that does not exist: the trace of an operator restricted to a subrepresentation, i.e. IsProj p P and f commuting with P entails trace (f.restrict) = trace (f * P). Two routes, both real work: prove that lemma, or define T, E, A as explicit representations with matrices given directly, which costs a sign cocycle for T and leaves the identification mirror-certified rather than kernel-certified.

ROADMAP B3 algebraic half. The character-level statement is delivered; the dimension statement dim Sym^2(R^3)^{B_3} = 1 needs the 48-element signed permutation group built as a Mathlib Representation the way Cubic.rho already is, after which A1 divides by the group order. This is plumbing of a kind already done once, which is why it ranks above A9.

Stinespring uniqueness in restricted form. Mathlib has no Stinespring dilation theorem, so the restricted statement has to be set up from the partial-trace side. High centrality because the substratum-is-gauge corollary and the whole universality-class story rest on it.

A clean finite-group statement -- entanglement-breaking iff t = s for an abelian Weyl subgroup of order 2^t on s qubits -- but Mathlib carries no entanglement-breaking characterization, so the definition has to be built before the theorem can be stated.
A rank bound on the off-diagonal blocks of a local update. Mathlib has matrix rank and the submatrix API; the content is that the block factors through the boundary index set.

Reciprocity of visible transition counts. The side condition is the interesting part and must be carried: the symmetric form T_ij = T_ji holds only for T-EVEN coarse states, and GR section 3.2 is explicit that with T-odd visible data only the (theta j, theta i) form survives.
Dimensional bookkeeping: [g] = (3-d)/2, dimensionless iff d = 3. Cheap, and it moves an SM GAP for almost nothing.
Needs non-degenerate spectra, non-vanishing overlaps and an argument over all t -- analytic, and the first GR statement worth attempting.

Already K1: the irreducible characters and their orthonormality are kernel-checked over the 24 rotations. Upgrading to K3 means stating the 4 = 1 + 3 branching as its own theorem rather than reading it off the table.
